items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
allowing certain members of the New York city police pension fund to borrow
from contributions
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6436

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
allowing certain members of the New York city police pension fund to
borrow from contributions

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA:

Relates to the restoration of rights for certain members of the New York
city police pension fund to borrow from their contributions to the fund.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

This bill amends paragraphs 1 and 2 of subsection b of section 517(c) of
the retirement and social security law to allow Tier 3 and 3R members of
the New York City Police Pension Fund ("PPF") as of January 1, 2018 to
borrow from contributions made to that fund under conditions consistent
with existing law allowing members of the State and Local Employee
retirement system to do the same.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, Tier 3 and 3R New York City PPF members are prohibited from
borrowing from their contributions pursuant to the Retirement and Social
Security Law ("RSSL") § 517 (c). Tier 1 and 2 members of the PPF are
permitted to borrow from their contributions. Other state and local
employees subject to RSSL Article 14, including those covered by the New
York State and Local Employees' Retirement System, the New York State
Employees Retirement System, the New York State Police and Fire Retire-
ment System, the New York State Teachers' Retirement System, the New
York City Teachers' Retirement System, the New York City Board of Educa-
tion Retirement System and certain members of the New York City Employ-
ees' Retirement System, are also permitted to borrow, pursuant to RSSL
§§ 517, 517-b, and 517-c.  The ability to take pension loans has long
been a significant benefit for police officers, who often use these
loans to assist them to fund educational expenses, a down payment on a
mortgage, or another vital need. The proposed legislation would restore
this important right in a manner that is consistent with the rights
available to police officers and other public employees throughout New
York City and New York State.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2022: S9327 - Referred to Civil Service & Pensions - Vetoed

2019: S5906B - Referred to Civil Service & Pensions

 
FISCAL IMPLICATION FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

See fiscal note.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
